summary: This guide covers importing RoleCall character cards and lorebooks, editing them in Bunzai, and exporting to RoleCall or another format. RoleCall cards add casting details, presentation settings, and sprites to the shared character fields. Bunzai reads character cards as PNG with embedded text or as JSON, and reads RoleCall lorebooks as JSON. The Library receipt reports what it recognized; card type detection uses file contents rather than the filename. The guide lists the fields available for editing and explains that parsed source data is retained as escrow. A same-format export preserves original field values and applies edits, while JSON formatting or the output container may change. Cross-format conversion carries shared character fields and drops RoleCall-specific extras when the target has no matching fields. Workbench saves preserve untouched field values semantically. The Press exports staged pieces to one chosen target, and linked lorebooks can travel with supported character cards. Common questions cover JSON output, portrait retention, RoleCall-only presentation data, and embedded lorebook editing and export.

sections.title: What Bunzai reads
sections.summary: Bunzai reads the two file types RoleCall gives you. Character cards arrive as PNG where RoleCall tucks card text inside the image or as plain JSON; both hold Character Card v2 or v3 with an extra block for casting card, presentation layer, and sprite pack. Lorebooks arrive as JSON in RoleCall's own export format. Drag the file onto the Library and drop anywhere in the room; Bunzai reads and shows a plain-words receipt of what it read and kept. It tells a RoleCall character card from a RoleCall persona card even though shapes are almost identical by reading inside the file for what marks a card as a character, not the filename or a guess. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

sections.title: What comes across cleanly
sections.summary: Bunzai retains the parsed source card data in escrow and exposes supported fields for editing: name, tagline, description, casting-card identity, personality, scenario, greetings, examples, prompts, creator details, tags, rating, genre, fandom, presentation settings, depth injections, sprites, and any embedded lorebook. The card image is retained as the portrait. The original data provides the basis for same-format export; changed canonical fields are applied when exporting. This describes parsed field data, not byte-for-byte retention of the source file, and the output may use different JSON formatting or a different container.

sections.title: What changes when you convert to another app
sections.summary: A same-format RoleCall export preserves the source card's field values and applies edits, but the JSON formatting or output container can change. During conversion to a different app, RoleCall-specific fields with no shared target home are dropped: casting-card details, presentation settings, rating, genre, fandom, and internal ids. Core character fields cross over as far as the target format supports them. Depth injections, sprites, and a linked lorebook are included only when the target provides a corresponding field or feature. The conversion keeps source-specific data in escrow rather than blindly copying it into another app's file. Where the target has fewer fields, the conversion report describes what it cannot represent.

sections.title: Editing on the Workbench
sections.summary: Open a Library piece in a Workbench tab to edit its name, description, personality, scenario, first message, and examples. Saving writes the RoleCall card with edits applied; untouched source field values remain semantically preserved, though serialized formatting may change in the output file.

sections.title: Exporting back out
sections.summary: Stage a piece for the Press by choosing Stage for the Press or dropping it from the Press rail. Each run exports staged pieces to one selected target format. RoleCall character cards are written as JSON, which RoleCall can import alongside PNG cards. A linked lorebook rides with the character when supported. Plain text or Markdown output is also available for reading. Choosing another app as the target applies the conversion rules: shared character fields cross over as supported, while RoleCall-only fields without a target equivalent remain in the original piece rather than being copied into the other format.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.summary: Does the card return exactly as it was? A RoleCall export preserves the original field values alongside edits, but JSON formatting or the output container may differ. Imported PNG cards export as JSON, which RoleCall can read. Bunzai retains the card art as the portrait and keeps source data in escrow. Casting-card and presentation fields stay with the RoleCall format and are not copied into unrelated app formats. An embedded lorebook can be edited separately and re-embedded when exporting to a format that supports it.
